claim: The largest saguaro on record was 78 feet (24 m) tall before it blew over in a storm in 1986.
corrected_claim: The tallest saguaro ever measured, an armless specimen near Cave Creek, Arizona, was 78 ft (23.8 m) tall before a windstorm toppled it in 1986.
quote: The tallest saguaro ever measured was an armless specimen found near Cave Creek, Arizona. It was 78 ft (23.8 m) in height before it was toppled in 1986 by a windstorm.
note: Page says tallest, not largest

claim: Hexagonal boron nitride is called 'white graphene' because of its similar structure to graphite, but it's an excellent electrical insulator and lubricant.
corrected_claim: Hexagonal boron nitride, nicknamed 'white graphite' for its graphite-like layers (thin sheets are sometimes called 'white graphene'), is an electrical insulator and a good lubricant at both low and high temperatures.
quote: Due to its analogous structure to that of graphene, atomically thin boron nitride is sometimes called white graphene. ... Unlike graphene, which is black and an electrical conductor, h-BN monolayer is white and an insulator. ... It is a good lubricant at both low and high temperatures
note: h-BN is 'white graphite'; 'white graphene' is for atomically thin BN

claim: Edgar Codd invented the relational database model at IBM in 1970 — IBM initially ignored his work, and Oracle implemented it first.
corrected_claim: Edgar Codd invented the relational database model while at IBM, publishing it in 1970, but IBM was slow to exploit it, and Oracle's database reached the market before IBM's own SQL/DS.
quote: To his disappointment, IBM proved slow to exploit his suggestions until commercial rivals started implementing them. ... in his Oracle Database, which actually reached the market before SQL/DS
note: IBM was slow rather than ignoring it; Oracle beat SQL/DS, page doesn't say it was first overall

claim: Circoviruses have circular single-stranded DNA — the smallest DNA genomes known in viruses.
corrected_claim: Circoviruses have tiny circular, non-segmented single-stranded DNA genomes only about 3.8 kb long, replicated by a rolling-circle mechanism.
quote: Genomes are circular and non-segmented, around 3.8kb in length. Replication follows the ssDNA rolling circle model.
note: 'Smallest DNA genomes known in viruses' not on page

claim: The critical period for accent-free second language acquisition ends around puberty — later learners usually retain an accent.
corrected_claim: Adult second-language learners nearly always retain an identifiable foreign accent, and some researchers place the end of the critical period at puberty, though some studies found older learners reaching native-like accents.
quote: adult second-language learners nearly always retain an immediately identifiable foreign accent ... Some research studies have considered the critical period to be any point before puberty
note: Puberty cutoff is one view among several; page cites counterevidence

claim: Cacti evolved their spines from leaves—modified leaves that reduce water loss and protect against herbivores.
quote: Most species of cacti have lost true leaves, retaining only spines, which are highly modified leaves. As well as defending against herbivores, spines help prevent water loss by reducing air flow close to the cactus and providing some shade.

claim: Cubic boron nitride is the second hardest material after diamond and is used to machine hardened steel because it doesn't react with iron like diamond does.
corrected_claim: Cubic boron nitride is only slightly softer than diamond, and it beats diamond for machining steel because it is insoluble in iron, while diamond dissolves in it.
quote: the hardness of bulk c-BN being slightly smaller and w-BN even higher than that of diamond ... c-BN surpasses diamond in mechanical applications, such as machining steel. Its usefulness arises from its insolubility in iron, nickel, and related alloys, whereas diamond is soluble in these metals.
note: Page doesn't rank it 'second hardest'; diamond is soluble in iron rather than 'reacting'

claim: Oracle was founded in 1977 to build the first commercial SQL database — the company was named after a CIA project the founders had worked on.
corrected_claim: Oracle was co-founded in 1977 as Software Development Laboratories, and its name came from the codename of a 1977 CIA project; the CIA was Oracle's first customer.
quote: co-founded Oracle on June 16, 1977, in Santa Clara, California, as Software Development Laboratories (SDL). ... The name also drew from the codename of a 1977 project for the Central Intelligence Agency, Oracle's first customer;
note: Page does not say it built the first commercial SQL database.

claim: Polioviruses infect through the intestine but cross into the nervous system — gut infection with neurological consequences.
corrected_claim: Poliovirus infects via the fecal–oral route and replicates in the gastrointestinal tract; paralytic disease occurs only when the virus enters the central nervous system and replicates in motor neurons.
quote: Infection occurs via the fecal–oral route, meaning that one ingests the virus ... viral replication occurs in the gastrointestinal tract. ... Paralytic disease occurs when the virus enters the central nervous system (CNS) and replicates in motor neurons
note: Nervous-system invasion happens only in a minority of cases, page calls it an accidental diversion
